attempts.label: DANDI:000007
attempts.paper_title: A cortico-cerebellar loop for motor planning
attempts.entry_title: A cortico-cerebellar loop for motor planning (Gao et al. 2018)
attempts.summary: The paper's findings on fastigial photo-activation held up in this data: it disrupted the mice's choices, abolished ALM selectivity and collapsed ALM preparatory activity along the coding direction with a lasting effect. The contrast with dentate photo-activation held only in part, as the dentate effect was small but not absent. Photo-inhibition of the cerebellar nuclei reduced ALM selectivity by 73% to 82% without abolishing it, and the number and latency of modulated ALM neurons did not match, partly because the files hold more neurons than the paper reports and do not say which it used. The cerebellar nuclei recordings, lesions and anatomy are not deposited, so the findings that rest on them could not be tested.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Gao, Davis, Thomas, Economo, Abrego, Svoboda, De Zeeuw and Li (2018) on its two deposits, DANDI:000007 and CRCNS:alm-4, which hold the same 54 ALM recording sessions of 13 mice during fastigial or dentate photo-activation and CN photo-inhibition. It tests the behavior in those sessions, ALM trial-type selectivity, ALM responses to CN photostimulation and the coding direction analysis. The lesion experiments, CN recordings, lick times, VGAT-ChR2 experiments and anatomy are not deposited.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Gao et al. (2018) from DANDI:000007 and CRCNS:alm-4
The findings of attempt gao-2018-01, checked on DANDI:000007 version 0.220126.1903

outcomes.statement: Fastigial nucleus lesions impair contralesional licking choices, measured as lower performance on trials instructing contralesional licking after the lesion than before.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 4; Figure 1d
outcomes.quote: Fastigial lesions impaired initiation of contralesional licking ( Fig 1d )
outcomes.notes: Neither dataset holds the lesion experiments. DANDI:000007 holds 54 ALM recording sessions and CRCNS:alm-4 the same 54 sessions (34 during CN photo-activation, 20 during CN photo-inhibition); the CRCNS descriptor lists no lesion data, and no other deposit is named by the paper.

outcomes.statement: Fastigial lesions slow the initiation of contralesional licking after the go cue, while lick rate within bouts and bout duration are unchanged.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 4; Figure 1e; Extended Data Figure 1b and 1c
outcomes.quote: slowed initiation of contralesional licking following the 'go' cue ( Fig 1e ). After movement initiation licking was unaffected
outcomes.notes: No lesion sessions and no lick times in either dataset (the trial tables give the outcome and an early-lick flag only; the CRCNS time series hold the laser command and power, not the lick contacts).

outcomes.statement: Dentate nucleus lesions do not change behavioral choice or movement execution.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 4; Figure 1d
outcomes.quote: Dentate lesions (~1.5 mm away) did not change behavioral choice and movement execution
outcomes.notes: No lesion sessions in either dataset; see fig1d-fastigial-lesion-contra-choice.

outcomes.statement: Fastigial photo-activation during the early sample epoch does not affect behavioral choice for either trial type.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: Fastigial photo-activation during the early sample epoch had no effect on behavioral choice (p>0.05 for either trial type, bootstrap, Methods)
outcomes.notes: Early sample photo-activation (code 1) against control in the 6 fastigial mice: contralateral trials 0.857 to 0.826 (change -0.031, one-sided bootstrap p = 0.36), ipsilateral 0.887 to 0.899 (+0.012, p = 0.37; one-sided p for a drop 0.64); pooled 0.870 to 0.861 (p = 0.42). Both p > 0.05. Without the four sessions whose laser traces disagree with their codes (MISMATCH in the notebook) p = 0.29 and 0.81. Trial-level checks, less conservative than the bootstrap, also find no drop (one-sided z-test p = 0.28, session-stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel p = 0.35).
deviations: Tested on the behavior of the ALM recording sessions (21 sessions, 6 mice), where photostimulation was on about a third of trials; the paper's Fig. 1g uses behavior sessions, which are not deposited. Supplemental Table 1 gives the same 6 mice for both.
Trials with GoodTrials = 0 or a NaN photostimulation code are left out, as in the deposited analysis scripts; the Methods do not mention them.

outcomes.statement: Fastigial photo-activation during the early delay epoch lowers behavioral performance, even though the photostimulus ends 800 ms before the movement.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 5; Figure 1g
outcomes.quote: Photo-activation during the delay and response epochs both resulted in incorrect choices ( Fig 1g–h ). Incorrect choices were induced even when the photostimuli ceased 800 ms before the movement
outcomes.notes: Early delay photo-activation (code 2; by the laser traces, light for 0.455 s from delay onset in the 2017 sessions, ending 0.845 s before the go cue, and 0.500 s in the 2015 sessions, ending 0.8 s before it, except 1.3 s, up to the go cue, in ANM314746_20151020) lowers pooled performance from 0.870 to 0.630 (change -0.240; no resample of 10,000 without a drop, p < 0.0001). Every mouse drops, by 0.083 to 0.450. Without the MISMATCH sessions 0.871 to 0.619 (p = 0.0004).
deviations: Behavior from the ALM recording sessions, not the behavior sessions of Fig. 1g.

outcomes.statement: Fastigial photo-activation during the delay epoch biases future movements toward either the contralateral or the ipsilateral direction, depending on the mouse.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 5; Figure 1h; Extended Data Figure 1e
outcomes.quote: Photo-activation during the delay epoch biased future movements to either the contralateral or ipsilateral direction in individual mice
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), early delay photo-activation. ANM314760 and BAYLORNL15 drop on contralateral trials (by 0.726 and 0.719, p < 0.0001) with no ipsilateral drop; ANM314746 and ANM314757 drop on ipsilateral trials (by 0.391, p = 0.003, and 0.221, p = 0.03), more than on contralateral trials. ANM314758 and BAYLORCD6 show neither significantly. Without the MISMATCH sessions the same four mice are biased (ipsilateral p = 0.018 and 0.005). Reading (b), the 1.255 s whole-delay experiment, is not in the datasets.
deviations: Recording-session behavior; reading (b) not testable.
Contra and ipsi are relative to the manipulated fastigial nucleus; for these mice the files' fiber side and the recorded ALM are on opposite sides, as the paper states.

outcomes.statement: Fastigial photo-activation during the response epoch produces a contralateral bias, opposite to the bias of fastigial lesions.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 5; Figure 1h; Extended Data Figure 1e
outcomes.quote: Photo-activation immediately before movement onset (response epoch) produced a contralateral bias ( Fig 1h ), opposite from the directional bias induced by fastigial lesions
outcomes.notes: The recording sessions have photo-activation only in the sample and delay epochs (codes 1 to 4); response-epoch photo-activation was in behavior sessions, which are not deposited.

outcomes.statement: Fastigial photo-activation does not block or change the frequency and duration of licking after a lick bout starts, and photo-activation in the delay does not evoke early licks.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 6; Figure 1i; Extended Data Figure 1f
outcomes.quote: Fastigial photo-activation did not block or perturb the frequency and duration of licking movements after initiation of licking bouts ( Fig 1i ). Fastigial photo-activation during the delay epoch did not evoke early licks
outcomes.notes: Lick times are in neither dataset (the CRCNS time series hold only the aom_input_trace and laser_power channels in all 54 sessions, though the descriptor says they record tongue movements), so lick rate within bouts and bout duration cannot be measured, and there is no response-epoch photo-activation. The early-lick part was tested from the per-trial LickEarly flag and holds pooled over mice, not in every mouse; the fraction of trials with an early lick is 0.083 in control and 0.130 with early delay photo-activation (two-sided bootstrap p = 0.33, 6 mice, 21 sessions; 0.322 without the MISMATCH sessions). Per mouse BAYLORCD6 licks early more (0.081 to 0.324, p < 0.0001; also 0.304 with sample photo-activation). Since the criterion needs all three measures and two cannot be taken, the claim stays blocked.

outcomes.statement: Dentate photo-activation produces little effect on behavioral choice.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 6; Figure 1g; Extended Data Figure 1e
outcomes.quote: Dentate photo-activation produced little effect on behavioral choice ( Fig 1g , p=0.06, bootstrap
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), early delay dentate photo-activation (code 4) in the 3 recorded dentate mice. On all 13 sessions pooled performance goes from 0.873 to 0.835 (change -0.039, one-sided bootstrap p = 0.107, paper p = 0.06), so the criterion's test finds no drop at p < 0.05; contralateral -0.055 (p = 0.09), ipsilateral -0.019 (p = 0.42). Without ANM314756_20151020 and BAYLORNL14_20170603, whose laser traces disagree with code 4 (0.78 s of light; 61% of code 4 trials lit at sample onset), it finds a drop (0.876 to 0.824, change -0.052, p = 0.042), and the trial-level checks find one on all sessions (z-test p = 0.007, stratified p = 0.016). The effect is small, as "little effect" says, but its absence at p < 0.05 depends on which sessions are kept, so the claim holds in part.
deviations: 3 of the paper's 8 dentate mice (the recorded ones), from recording sessions; reading (b), the 1.255 s photostimulus, is not in the datasets.
The main analysis keeps the sessions whose laser traces disagree with their codes, as the lab's scripts use the codes; the variant without them is shown beside it.

outcomes.statement: Photostimulating Purkinje cells in L7-cre x Ai32 mice silences fastigial nucleus neurons, while photostimulation over the inferior colliculus does not.
outcomes.source: Methods, CN photo-inhibition, paragraph 1; Figure 1j; Extended Data Figure 2c and 2d
outcomes.quote: Photostimulation of the cerebellar cortex silenced fastigial activity whereas photostimulation of the inferior colliculus did not
outcomes.notes: CN recordings are in neither dataset; both hold ALM units only.

outcomes.statement: Fastigial photo-inhibition during the early sample epoch does not affect behavioral choice.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 7; Figure 1k
outcomes.quote: Photo-inhibition during the early sample epoch did not affect behavioral choice ( Fig 1k , p>0.05 for either trial type, bootstrap, Methods)
outcomes.notes: The photo-inhibition recording sessions have delay photo-inhibition only (codes 5 and 6); the behavior sessions with sample-epoch photo-inhibition are not deposited.

outcomes.statement: Fastigial photo-inhibition during the late sample and the delay epochs causes incorrect choices, with a larger effect in the delay epoch.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 7; Figure 1k; Extended Data Figure 2g and 2h
outcomes.quote: Photo-inhibition during the late sample and delay epochs resulted in incorrect behavioral choices, with a larger effect induced in the delay epoch

statistics.about: sub-epoch photo-inhibition, the weaker effect marked
sub-epoch photo-inhibition, the stronger effect marked

outcomes.notes: Late-sample and late-delay photo-inhibition are not in the datasets. The early-delay 0.5 s photo-inhibition of the recording sessions (code 5) lowers pooled performance from 0.848 to 0.706 (one-sided bootstrap p = 0.014, 4 mice), shown in the fig1k-inhibition-delay-bias section.

outcomes.statement: Fastigial photo-inhibition during the delay epoch biases future movements to the contralateral or the ipsilateral direction, depending on the mouse.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 7; Extended Data Figure 2g and 2h
outcomes.quote: Photo-inhibition during the delay epoch biased future movements to either the contralateral or ipsilateral direction in individual mice
outcomes.notes: Reading (b), 1.3 s delay photo-inhibition (code 6): with contra and ipsi from the paper's rule (CN contralateral to the recorded ALM), BAYLORCD12 and BAYLORCD13 drop on contralateral trials (by 0.464, p = 0.002, and 0.385, p = 0.009) and BAYLORCD14 on ipsilateral trials (0.234, p = 0.008); with the files' CN side the labels of CD12, CD13 and CD14 swap, giving 1 contra- and 2 ipsi-biased mice. Both give mice biased each way. Reading (a), 0.5 s early delay (code 5), gives 0 contra- and 2 ipsi-biased mice under the paper's rule, 1 and 1 under the files' side.
deviations: The 4 recorded L7-cre x Ai32 mice (CD8, CD12, CD13, CD14) from recording sessions, in place of the 3 (CD12, CD13, CD16) and 7 behavior mice of Extended Data Fig. 2g and 2h; late-delay photo-inhibition is not deposited.
The files put the fastigial fiber on the same side as the recorded ALM for CD12, CD13 and CD14, against the paper's contralateral design; both side assignments were run and both reproduce.

outcomes.statement: Fastigial photo-inhibition during the response epoch produces an ipsilateral bias, as fastigial lesions do and opposite to photo-activation.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 7; Figure 1k; Extended Data Figure 2g
outcomes.quote: Photo-inhibition during movement initiation (response epoch) produced an ipsilateral bias ( Fig 1k ), consistent with fastigial lesions, and opposite from the bias induced by fastigial photo-activation
outcomes.notes: No response-epoch photo-inhibition in the recording sessions; behavior sessions are not deposited.

outcomes.statement: Fastigial photo-inhibition minimally affects movement execution, and at the intensities of the task evokes no consistent movement.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 7; Figure 1l; Extended Data Figure 2e, 2f and 2i; Methods, CN photo-inhibition and effects on movement
outcomes.quote: Photo-inhibition minimally affected movement execution ( Fig 1l ). No other movements were consistently evoked during photo-inhibition
outcomes.notes: No lick times, no video or jaw tracking, and no response-epoch photo-inhibition in either dataset, so the lick-bout part cannot be tested. The early-lick part was tested from the LickEarly flag in the 4 recorded mice (the criterion names 7 behavior mice) and holds pooled over mice, not in every mouse; 0.109 in control against 0.164 with 0.5 s delay photo-inhibition (two-sided bootstrap p = 0.13) and 0.112 against 0.068 with 1.3 s photo-inhibition (p = 0.22). Per mouse BAYLORCD8 licks early more with code 5 (0.083 to 0.209, p = 0.008) and less with code 6 (0.090 to 0.011, p < 0.0001). The claim stays blocked, as the lick-bout part is missing.

outcomes.statement: In VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice, fastigial photostimulation in the early delay reduces performance on both trial types (contra lick 74.5% to 58.5%, ipsi lick 67.8% to 57.0%).
outcomes.source: Methods, ALM photo-inhibition after a fastigial perturbation, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: fastigial perturbations during the early delay epoch reduced behavioral performance for both trial types (control ... 74.5% correct, "ipsi lick" trials, 67.8%; photostimulation ... 58.5% and 57.0%; p<0.05 for both trial types, bootstrap)
outcomes.notes: The VGAT-ChR2-EYFP behavior is in neither dataset (the 13 mice are wild type or L7-cre x Ai32).

outcomes.statement: Most ALM putative pyramidal neurons (980 of 1194) distinguish "lick left" from "lick right" trials in their spike counts.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 9; Methods, Electrophysiology data analysis
outcomes.quote: Most ALM pyramidal neurons distinguished "lick left" and "lick right" trials in spike counts (980/1194, p<0.05, two-tailed t-test, Methods)
outcomes.notes: In the 34 photo-activation sessions, 856 of 1084 pyramidal neurons are selective (0.790) with correct trials and a 1.3 s response window, the reading of the deposited Fig. 2 script; 0.797 with 1.5 s, 0.740 and 0.744 with correct and error trials. All four readings are within 0.82 +- 0.082. By mouse 0.63 to 0.86. On the DANDI trial set (which lacks trials in two sessions) 842 of 1084 (0.777). The counts are not judged, as the datasets hold 34 of the 39 sessions. The t-test on spike counts (the wording of E2) in place of rates gives the same 856, and the lab's compiled file analysis_compile_all_ALM_data.mat holds the same 1084 pyramidal units with the same verdict for every one (856 marked selective).
deviations: 34 of the 39 sessions (9 of 10 mice); the tenth mouse, excluded from the photo-activation analyses, is not deposited.

The response window (1.3 s from the go cue) and the trial set (correct trials) are from the deposited script analysis_compile_all_ALM_data.m; the Methods do not give them. Both readings of each were run.

outcomes.statement: A proportion of CN neurons similar to ALM (416 of 564) shows trial-type selectivity.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 9
outcomes.quote: A similar proportion of CN neurons showed trial-type selectivity (416/564)
outcomes.notes: CN recordings are in neither dataset.

outcomes.statement: Preparatory activity (selectivity before the response epoch) is more prevalent in ALM (59% of neurons) than in the CN (35%).
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 9
outcomes.quote: Preparatory activity (selectivity before the response epoch) was more prevalent in ALM (ALM, 59% of neurons, CN, 35%; p<0.001, chi-square test)
outcomes.notes: ALM only, as the criterion allows when the CN neurons are missing. 610 of 1084 pyramidal neurons (0.563) are selective in the sample or delay epoch with correct trials, 0.538 with correct and error trials; both within 0.59 +- 0.059. As a fraction of selective neurons, 0.71 to 0.73, outside. The CN fraction and the chi-square comparison cannot be computed, so the comparison the claim makes is untested; the outcome records that only the ALM half could be shown, as for fig2-peri-movement-equal. Measured is the ALM fraction.
deviations: CN half not deposited.

outcomes.statement: Peri-movement activity (selectivity in the response epoch) is equally prevalent in ALM (67%) and the CN (66%).
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 9
outcomes.quote: Peri-movement activity (selectivity during response epoch) was equally prevalent in both regions (ALM, 67%, CN, 66%)
outcomes.notes: The ALM half holds; 696 of 1084 pyramidal neurons (0.642) are selective in the response epoch with correct trials and a 1.3 s window (0.636 with 1.5 s), within 0.67 +- 0.067; with correct and error trials 0.562 to 0.571, outside. The CN half, and so the equality the claim states, cannot be tested; the outcome records that only part of the claim could be shown.
deviations: CN half not deposited.

outcomes.statement: In both ALM and the CN, a similar small proportion of neurons (under 10%) modulates its spike rate during individual licks.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 9; Extended Data Figure 4a to 4c
outcomes.quote: In both regions, a similar proportion (<10%) of neurons modulated their spike rates during individual licks
outcomes.notes: Lick times are in neither dataset, and CN recordings are not deposited.

outcomes.statement: Selectivity for "lick left" and "lick right" trials emerges gradually in both the ALM and the CN population averages, starting during the sample epoch and peaking in the response epoch.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 10; Figure 2c and 2d
outcomes.quote: Selectivity for "lick left" and "lick right" trials emerged gradually in both ALM and CN population averages ( Fig 2c–d ), starting during the sample epoch and reaching a maximum at the response epoch
outcomes.notes: ALM, reading (a), 827 selective neurons: the bootstrap interval excludes zero from 0.13 s after sample onset (117 of 129 sample-epoch points), the mean is 0.65 spikes/s in the sample, 1.80 in the delay and 1.91 in the response epoch, and the maximum (2.37) is 0.23 s after the go cue; all three conditions hold. Reading (b), 591 neurons, peaks 0.06 s before the go cue. The CN half of the claim cannot be tested.
deviations: CN half not deposited.
Preferred type from 10 correct control trials of each type and neurons with more than 15 trials of each type, from the deposited Fig. 2 script; PSTHs with its 200 ms boxcar, on a 10 ms grid.

outcomes.statement: Most CN neurons with delay selectivity predict the upcoming licking direction, not object location (67%), switching their preference on error trials.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 10; Extended Data Figure 4e
outcomes.quote: However, most CN neurons predicted the upcoming licking direction (67%, Extended Data Fig 4 ), similar to ALM
outcomes.notes: CN recordings are in neither dataset.

outcomes.statement: Preparatory activity is present in all three cerebellar nuclei (fastigial, interposed and dentate).
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 11; Extended Data Figure 4f
outcomes.quote: Preparatory activity was present in all three cerebellar nuclei ( Extended Data Fig 3 – 4 )
outcomes.notes: CN recordings are in neither dataset.

outcomes.statement: In the fastigial nucleus, equal numbers of neurons prefer contralateral and ipsilateral movement in the early delay, and a population preference for contralateral movement develops just before movement initiation.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 11; Extended Data Figure 4g
outcomes.quote: equal numbers of neurons preferred either contralateral or ipsilateral movement during the early delay, and a population-level preference for contralateral movement developed right before movement initiation

statistics.about: the mark on the fastigial late delay proportion (the legend does not name the bar)

outcomes.notes: CN recordings are in neither dataset.

outcomes.statement: Bilateral ALM photo-inhibition during the delay rapidly alters the activity of many CN neurons (185 of 389), with a latency of 10.7 plus or minus 4.0 ms.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 12; Figure 3a and 3b; Extended Data Figure 5a
outcomes.quote: Activity of many CN neurons was rapidly altered by ALM photo-inhibition (185/389, p<0.01, two-tailed t-test; latency, 10.7 ± 4.0 ms, mean ± s.e.m.)
outcomes.notes: CN recordings during ALM photo-inhibition are in neither dataset.

outcomes.statement: ALM photo-inhibition makes more CN neurons increase than decrease their activity (123 against 62 of 185), a net disinhibition of the CN.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 12; Figure 3b
outcomes.quote: Photo-inhibiting ALM caused a greater proportion of CN neurons to increase their activity, resulting in net disinhibition of CN ( Fig 3b , 123/185 increase, 62/185 decrease, p<0.001, binomial test)
outcomes.notes: CN recordings are in neither dataset; depends on fig3-cn-altered-by-alm-inhibition.

outcomes.statement: ALM photo-inhibition abolishes CN selectivity for "lick left" and "lick right" trials.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 12; Figure 3c; Extended Data Figure 5b to 5d
outcomes.quote: CN selectivity for "lick left" and "lick right" trials was abolished by photo-inhibiting ALM
outcomes.notes: CN recordings are in neither dataset.

outcomes.statement: Photo-inhibiting either hemisphere of ALM reduces CN preparatory activity, and photo-inhibiting motor cortex posterior to ALM has less effect.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 13; Extended Data Figure 6a to 6e
outcomes.quote: Photo-inhibiting either side of ALM reduced CN preparatory activity ( Extended Data Fig 6a–d ). Photo-inhibiting motor cortex regions posterior to ALM produced less effect on CN preparatory activity
outcomes.notes: CN recordings are in neither dataset.

outcomes.statement: CN photo-inhibition during the delay rapidly alters the activity of many ALM neurons (197 of 454), with a latency of 7.1 plus or minus 3.8 ms.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 14; Figure 3d and 3e; Extended Data Figure 5e
outcomes.quote: Activity of many ALM neurons was rapidly altered by CN photo-inhibition (197/454, p<0.01, two-tailed t-test, Extended Data Fig 5e ; latency, 7.1 ± 3.8 ms)
outcomes.notes: With 1.3 s delay photo-inhibition (19 sessions, 4 mice), 228 of 486 tested pyramidal neurons change their delay rate (0.469; correct trials only, 106 of 263, 0.403). The count of 228 (or 106) is outside 197 +- 19.7. The latency is 15.3 +- 12.9 ms (bootstrap mean and s.d., bin start, all trials) and 31.7 ms with correct trials; 20 to 42 ms when bins are labelled by centre or end. No reading reaches 7.1 +- 3.8 ms. The fraction, 0.469, is within 10% of 0.43, but the criterion uses the fraction only where the dataset holds fewer neurons, and here it holds more (682 pyramidal neurons against 454; the lab's compiled file for these sessions holds the same 737 units and 682 pyramidal neurons as the deposits). By mouse the modulated fraction is 0.16 (CD12) to 0.55 (CD8). The clock check (selectivity onset at sample onset, shifted with the trial events) holds in the photo-inhibition sessions, so the long latency is not a misalignment of spikes and trial events larger than its 200 ms windows.
deviations: The files hold 682 pyramidal neurons in the photo-inhibition sessions where the paper reports 454; the count is judged as the criterion says, and the fraction is reported.

Neurons tested need at least 8 control trials of each type and more than 3 photo-inhibition trials of each type, and early-lick trials are left out, as the deposited FR script; the Methods give neither.
Latency bins are labelled by their start, centre or end, which the paper does not state; all three are shown.

outcomes.statement: Despite the changes in individual neurons, the average ALM spike rate is nearly unchanged by CN photo-inhibition (4.15 against 4.39 spikes/s).
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 14
outcomes.quote: However, the average spike rate was nearly unchanged (control: 4.15 spikes/s; photo-inhibition: 4.39 spikes/s; p=0.58, two-tailed t-test)
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), all 486 tested pyramidal neurons, all trials: delay rate 4.03 spikes/s in control and 4.21 with CN photo-inhibition (change +0.18), paired t-test p = 0.51, unpaired p = 0.66; both rates within tolerance and no difference. Reading (b), the 228 modulated neurons: 5.52 and 6.20 (p = 0.25 and 0.35). With correct trials only, 3.27 and 3.85 (p = 0.08 and 0.24).

outcomes.statement: Among ALM neurons modulated by CN photo-inhibition, 108 increase and 89 decrease their responses.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 14; Figure 3e
outcomes.quote: Individual ALM neurons increased (108/197) or decreased (89/197) their responses during CN photo-inhibition
outcomes.notes: Of the 228 modulated neurons, 122 increase and 106 decrease, above 108 +- 10.8 and 89 +- 8.9; with correct trials 65 and 41. The increase fraction with all trials, 0.535, is within 10% of 0.55 (0.613 with correct trials, outside), but the criterion uses the fraction only where the dataset holds fewer neurons, and the files hold more (682 pyramidal neurons against 454).
deviations: The files hold more neurons than the paper reports for these mice; the counts are judged as the criterion says and the fraction is reported.

outcomes.statement: CN photo-inhibition abolishes ALM trial-type selectivity.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 14; Figure 3f
outcomes.quote: ALM trial-type selectivity was abolished by CN photo-inhibition ( Fig 3f )
outcomes.notes: 336 selective neurons tested on more than 3 trials in all conditions. Whole delay: control 1.46 spikes/s [1.14, 1.82], photo-inhibition 0.39 [0.19, 0.60]; last 500 ms: 1.52 [1.12, 1.96] and 0.27 [0.02, 0.53]. Selectivity falls by 73% to 82% but its interval excludes zero in both windows, so it is not abolished by the criterion. With 5 screening trials (the deposited script) 0.37 [0.17, 0.57] and 0.32 [0.06, 0.56].
deviations: The criterion's 10 screening trials per type are from the Methods; the deposited script uses 5, shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: Fastigial projections overlap ALM-projecting thalamus (VM and parts of VAL) more than dentate projections, which target a more dorsal and lateral region.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 15; Figure 4b and 4c; Extended Data Figure 7d to 7f
outcomes.quote: Fastigial projections mostly overlapped with parts of the thalamus that project to ALM (i.e., ventral medial nucleus, VM, and parts of anterior-lateral nucleus, VAL), whereas dentate projections targeted an adjacent region that was more dorsal and lateral
outcomes.notes: The anatomy (injections and sections) is in neither dataset.

outcomes.statement: ALM-projecting thalamus receives inputs from the SNr and the lateral superior colliculus with overlaps comparable to the fastigial nucleus, while dentate overlap is lower.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Figure 8b
outcomes.quote: Fastigial, SNr, and superior colliculus labeling show comparable amount of overlaps with ALM-projecting thalamus. Dentate labeling show less overlap
outcomes.notes: The anatomy is in neither dataset.

outcomes.statement: Fastigial photo-activation changes ALM activity rapidly (latency 4.5 plus or minus 2.6 ms), consistent with a disynaptic pathway through the thalamus.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 16; Extended Data Figure 9a
outcomes.quote: Fastigial photo-activation induced rapid changes in ALM activity (latency, 4.5 ± 2.6 ms; Extended Data Fig 9a ), consistent with a disynaptic pathway through the thalamus
outcomes.notes: Neurons modulated in the 0.455 s photostimulation window, all trials, bins labelled by start: latency 3.6 +- 2.9 ms, within 4.5 +- 2.6. Labelled by centre it is 8.6 ms, outside; with the whole delay as window 7.8 ms. The count is 177 of 445 tested (whole-delay window 187, correct trials 67 to 68, without the script's minimum trial counts 190 of 538), against 227 +- 22.7 from the same 6 mice; the count does not reproduce. By mouse 11 to 66 modulated neurons. The tested set is the lab's (its compiled FR file has p-values for the same 445 pyramidal neurons; its 400 ms-bin p-values equal those here to 3e-13 where it has a value, and its NaN entries are 1.0 here; the window p-values were not compared). Without the MISMATCH sessions 166 of 401 are modulated and the latency is 4.22 ms by bin start (9.22 by centre). A bin labelled by its start holds spikes up to 10 ms later, so this label gives the earliest time the effect could begin in its bin.
deviations: The latency match rests on labelling each 10 ms bin by its start (assumed); the paper does not say how a bin is placed in time, and the centre and end labels give 8.6 and 13.6 ms.
Minimum trial counts and early-lick exclusion from the deposited FR script.

outcomes.statement: Fastigial photo-activation abolishes selective persistent and ramping activity in most ALM neurons, while in a minority it creates new preparatory activity.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 16; Figure 4e; Extended Data Figure 9c
outcomes.quote: Selective persistent and ramping activity was abolished in most ALM neurons ( Fig 4e , top). In a minority of neurons, photo-activation created new preparatory activity
outcomes.notes: 328 selective neurons tested on more than 3 trials in all conditions, as Extended Data Fig. 9c. From light offset to the go cue the population selectivity is 2.20 spikes/s [1.67, 2.79] in control and 0.66 [0.31, 1.03] with photo-activation (difference 1.55 [1.01, 2.09]); 163 of the 183 neurons selective in control lose significance (0.89) and 6 gain it. In the last 500 ms, 157 of 174 lose it and 9 gain it. With 5 screening trials the difference is 1.20 [0.66, 1.78]. The loss is not explained by the fewer photo-activation trials; with control trials subsampled to the photo-activation counts of each type (100 subsamples), 0.86 (light offset to go cue) and 0.89 (last 500 ms) of the control-selective neurons still lose significance and 16.3 and 18.6 gain it, against 0.51 and 0.52 losing and 35.4 and 30.1 gaining under dentate photo-activation. Without the MISMATCH sessions, 151 of 165 lose it and 6 gain it, difference 1.83 [1.28, 2.43].
deviations: The per-neuron test (E2 t-test on the window) is the claims file's choice; the paper gives none.

outcomes.statement: Transient fastigial photo-activation alters ALM preparatory activity long (more than 1 s) after the photostimulus ends.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 16; Figure 4f; Extended Data Figure 9b
outcomes.quote: Transient photo-activation of the fastigial nucleus altered ALM preparatory activity long (>1 s) after cessation of the photostimulus
outcomes.notes: In 400 ms bins starting 1 s or more after light offset (all in the response epoch), a mean 0.1345 of 445 neurons change their rate at p < 0.01, against 1% (binomial p = 3e-47) and against 0.0092 in the bins before light onset (z = 7.27, p = 2e-13). The fraction peaks at 0.42 during the light and stays at 0.12 to 0.14 up to 2 s after the go cue. These bins lie in the response epoch, where photo-activation changes the mix of licks; within the licked direction the fraction is 0.127 ("lick right", 399 neurons) and 0.072 ("lick left", 286), above 1% (p = 3e-39 and 3e-12) and above before onset (p = 3e-10 and 0.0016). Without the MISMATCH sessions 0.1457. The per-bin p-values equal those in the lab's compiled FR file (p_stim2_FN) to 3e-13 wherever it has a value; its 381 NaN entries are 1.0 here, so neither counts them significant.

outcomes.statement: Dentate photo-activation also changes ALM responses (latency 8.3 plus or minus 5.0 ms), but ALM activity recovers quickly after it.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 16; Figure 4g; Extended Data Figure 9a
outcomes.quote: Dentate photo-activation also induced ALM response changes ( Fig 4g ; latency, 8.3 ± 5.0 ms). Importantly, activity quickly recovered after dentate photo-activation
outcomes.notes: Stimulation window, all trials, bins labelled by start as in fig4-fastigial-activation-alm-latency: latency 3.3022 +- 3.07 ms, just inside 3.3 to 13.3, and 172 modulated neurons of 517, both within tolerance (by centre 8.30 ms, also within; whole-delay window 146 neurons). After the light the fraction of significant neurons falls from 0.33 to 0.0476 in the bins 1 s or more after offset, lower than fastigial (0.1345, one-sided p = 1e-6), but still above 1% (binomial p = 2e-10) and above the 0.0147 before light onset (p = 0.0013). The recovery test fails under both comparisons, so the claim holds in part. Without the MISMATCH sessions 0.0475 (p = 6e-9 against 1%, 0.0007 against before onset), latency 3.62 ms by start (8.62 by centre) with 166 modulated neurons. Within the licked direction 0.036 ("lick right") and 0.027 ("lick left"), above 1% in both (p = 7e-6 and 8e-4); against before onset p = 0.024 and 0.098.
deviations: The latency match rests on labelling each 10 ms bin by its start (assumed), the label used for the fastigial latency; the paper does not say how a bin is placed in time. The start label matches both latencies, the dentate one at the lower bound; the centre label also matches the dentate latency (8.30 ms), not the fastigial one.

outcomes.statement: In control trials, ALM activity trajectories for "lick left" and "lick right" diverge along the coding direction during the sample epoch and stay separated through the delay epoch.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 17; Figure 4h and 4i
outcomes.quote: In control trials, activity trajectories from "lick left" and "lick right" trials diverged from each other along the cd during the sample epoch and remained separated throughout the delay epoch
outcomes.notes: 20 sessions (8 to 46 neurons). The separation of independent control trials along the cd excludes zero from 2.06 s before the go cue, in 75 of 130 sample-epoch windows, and in all 131 windows centred in the delay (smallest lower bound 5.98). Before sample onset it is -0.13. The lab's compiled CD file lists 23 sessions (8 to 46 neurons, the range the Methods give for 28 sessions); the 20 here are among them, and the 3 others have at most 5 trials in some condition here.
deviations: 20 of 34 sessions pass the neuron rule of the deposited CD script (stable from the 50th trial to the 50th before the end); the paper used 28 of 39. The rule is the script's; the Methods give only "> 5 neurons for > 5 trials per condition".
The cd uses correct trials of a random half of control trials; the paper does not say how the trials are split (the claims file names this split as a standard choice).

outcomes.statement: Fastigial photo-activation collapses ALM activity trajectories along the coding direction, while dentate photo-activation minimally affects them.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 17; Figure 4i; Extended Data Figure 9c
outcomes.quote: Fastigial photo-activation resulted in a collapse of activity trajectories ... In contrast, dentate photo-activation minimally impacted activity trajectories along the cd , despite having an impact on ALM neuron responses
outcomes.notes: Fastigial (8 sessions), last 400 ms: control 18.39 [10.05, 27.12], photo-activation 6.09 [0.26, 14.46], difference 12.30 [5.84, 20.91], 67% of control; reading (b) holds and reading (a) does not (interval above zero). Dentate (12 sessions): 14.68 against 12.62, difference 2.07 [0.15, 4.18], 14% of control; the interval of the difference excludes zero, so the dentate condition of the criterion fails. From light offset to the go cue the same: fastigial -69%, dentate -18% [0.75, 4.65]. The contrast the claim states is present, but the dentate effect is not nil. With the lab's session rule (>= 3 trials per condition, the 23 sessions of its CD compile) the same (fastigial photo-activation [2.31, 11.88], dentate difference [0.26, 4.24]). Without the MISMATCH sessions both conditions hold in the last 400 ms (fastigial [-0.67, 5.72], dentate difference [-0.41, 4.25], 7 and 10 sessions) but not from light offset to the go cue (dentate [0.34, 4.97]); the outcome is the one on all sessions, as the lab's scripts use the codes.
deviations: 8 fastigial and 12 dentate sessions pass the session rule (see fig4i-cd-control-separation).

outcomes.statement: The projection along the coding direction captures 64.1% of ALM population selectivity over the sample and delay epochs and 27.0% of the total variance in task-related activity.
outcomes.source: Methods, Analysis of ALM population dynamics in the activity space, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: The projection along the cd captured 64.1±3.4% of the population selectivity for "lick left" and "lick right" trials over the sample and delay epochs (root mean square, RMS, of the spike rate difference between "lick right" and "lick left" trials), and 27.0±4.2% of the total variance in ALM task-related activity
outcomes.notes: Reading (b), squared ratios, with the selectivity measured on held-out correct control trials: 66.3% (s.e.m. 5.0), within 64.1 +- 3.4 (73.4% on the cd-estimating trials, outside). The variance of task-related activity, taken as the activity of the condition means, is 35.9% (held out) and 38.7% (cd-estimating trials) under reading (b) and 56.0% and 58.9% under (a), all outside 27.0 +- 4.2. The selectivity part holds under one reading and the variance part under none, so the claim holds in part. Only variance over single trials (28.4% and 29.4%) falls within tolerance; that variant is not a reading of the claims file, and the lab's CD script declares the variance measures but does not compute them.
deviations: Assumed that the selectivity is measured on correct control trials independent of those that estimated the cd (the projections of E6 use independent trials); on the cd-estimating trials it is 73.4%, outside, and the claim would not be reproduced. Activity variance is taken over the condition means, as "task-related activity" reads; the single-trial variant is shown only for comparison.

outcomes.statement: In the ALM recording sessions, contralateral fastigial photo-activation lowers behavioral performance, with "lick left" and "lick right" trials pooled, in the 6 mice.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Figure 10a and 10b
outcomes.quote: Performance in control (grey) and photostimulation trials (cyan). "Lick left" and "lick right" trials are pooled. Chance is 50% (dashed line). Lines, individual mice (ALM photo-inhibition, n=7; fastigial photo-activation, n=6). ***, p<0.001, one-sided test, bootstrap (Methods).
outcomes.notes: 6 mice, 21 sessions: pooled performance 0.870 in control and 0.630 with early delay photo-activation; no resample of 10,000 without a drop (p < 0.0001 < 0.001).

outcomes.statement: After bilateral ALM photo-inhibition in the early delay, the distance of ALM trajectories to the endpoints along the coding direction still predicts the future movement, though performance is near chance.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Information, page 1, paragraph 1; Extended Data Figure 10b and 10c
outcomes.quote: But in a trial-by-trial analysis movement direction could still be predicted based on the distance of the perturbed activity trajectories to the endpoints on the cd

statistics.about: performance drop with bilateral ALM photo-inhibition

outcomes.notes: Neither dataset has ALM photo-inhibition trials (the codes are 0 to 6, CN photostimulation only), and no VGAT-ChR2 mouse is deposited.

outcomes.statement: After fastigial photo-activation, the distance of ALM trajectories to the endpoints along the coding direction no longer predicts future movements.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Information, page 1, paragraph 1; Extended Data Figure 10d
outcomes.quote: After fastigial photo-activation, the distance of the perturbed trajectories to these endpoints no longer predicted future movements
outcomes.notes: 181 fastigial photo-activation trials with a lick in 8 sessions. The projection on the cd in the last 400 ms of the delay still predicts the lick direction (logistic slope 0.54 per s.d. [0.19, 0.90], p = 0.003); the probability of licking right is 0.43, 0.49, 0.47 and 0.73 by projection quartile. On control trials the slope is 1.85 [1.55, 2.15] (0.16 to 0.92 by quartile). The prediction is weaker after photo-activation but not absent. Without the MISMATCH sessions the slope is 0.38 [0.03, 0.74] (p = 0.035, 163 trials, 7 sessions); with the lab's 23 sessions (11 fastigial) 0.30 [0.02, 0.58] (p = 0.038, 220 trials).
deviations: The projection is not converted to a distance to endpoints; the criterion fits lick direction on the projection itself.
8 fastigial sessions pass the session rule (see fig4i-cd-control-separation).

outcomes.statement: Unilateral ALM photo-inhibition before the go cue biases licking ipsilaterally whether or not a fastigial perturbation preceded it, and bilateral ALM photo-inhibition during movement initiation raises the no-lick rate even after a fastigial perturbation.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Information, page 1, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 10e to 10g
outcomes.quote: Unilateral ALM photo-inhibition before movement initiation biased upcoming movements to the ipsilateral direction regardless of a preceding fastigial perturbation (Extended Data Fig 10e-f). Bilateral ALM photo-inhibition during movement initiation led to an increased no lick rate even after a preceding fastigial perturbation

unilateral ALM photo-inhibition after fastigial perturbation, weaker mark
unilateral ALM photo-inhibition after fastigial perturbation, stronger mark
no lick rate, bilateral ALM photo-inhibition, weaker mark
no lick rate, bilateral ALM photo-inhibition, stronger mark

outcomes.notes: The VGAT-ChR2-EYFP experiments are in neither dataset.

findings.statement: Both datasets hold only the ALM recordings during CN photo-activation (34 sessions, 9 mice) and CN photo-inhibition (20 sessions, 4 mice). The lesion experiments, the behavior-only sessions (including response-epoch and 1.3 s photostimulation), the 878 CN units, lick times, video, the VGAT-ChR2-EYFP experiments, the anatomy, and the tenth mouse of the Fig. 2 ALM recordings are not deposited; 24 of the 46 claims in the claims file cannot be tested.

DANDI:000007 lacks trials that CRCNS:alm-4 holds with GoodTrials = 1 and a valid photostimulation code; ANM314746 2015-10-22 has 258 of 284 (trials 279 to 304, the last 26 such trials, missing) and ANM314757 2015-10-21 has 34 of 302 (trials 48 to 315 missing); in both, DANDI holds no trial after the first missing one. In the other 52 sessions DANDI holds exactly those trials, with the same codes and outcomes, and every unit's spike times are identical.

In DANDI:000007 the trial columns cue_time and pole_in_time are described as relative to the trial start, but hold session times; trial start times are rounded (they differ from CRCNS:alm-4 by up to 0.05 s).

For the photo-inhibition mice BAYLORCD12, BAYLORCD13 and BAYLORCD14 both datasets give the photostimulation site as the left fastigial nucleus and the ALM recording at ML -1.5 mm (left), on the same side (DANDI: optogenetics hemisphere left, ML -0.8 mm; electrode group ML -1.5 mm; for BAYLORCD8 right and -1.5 mm), while the paper, the CRCNS descriptor and the trial code descriptions say the CN was manipulated contralateral to the recorded ALM; Supplemental Table 1 lists BAYLORCD14 as recorded in right ALM. Which side was manipulated cannot be told from the files.

In DANDI:000007 the trial column photo_stim_id has no description beyond its type ("varchar(8) #") in all 54 files, and no file holds a laser or photostimulation trace (acquisition, stimulus and processing are empty). The codes are 1 and 2 in the fastigial, 3 and 4 in the dentate and 5 and 6 in the L7-cre x Ai32 sessions; which epoch, duration and power each stands for is not given in the files.

In DANDI:000007 the subjects anm00314746, anm00314756, anm00314757, anm00314758 and anm00314760 carry no other identifier, where the paper names these mice AN105 to AN109. By site, anm00314756 (the one dentate mouse of the five) and anm00314757 (the one with a left fastigial site and right ALM) can be matched; anm00314746, anm00314758 and anm00314760 share a right fastigial site and left ALM and cannot. The genotype of every mouse that is not L7-cre x Ai32 is "unknown", and session_description is empty in all 54 files.

In DANDI:000007 the units' cell_type column labels 60 units "pyramidal" whose mean waveform has a trough-to-peak width under the paper's 0.45 ms (33 under 0.35 ms), and 3 units "unknown". Every unit's waveform sampling rate is given as 20000 Hz, including the 34 sessions recorded with the 32-channel NeuroNexus probe, which the Methods say were sampled at 25,000 Hz; in 14 of those sessions the mean waveforms have 37 or 38 samples, against 30 in every other session.

In 2 of the 54 sessions of DANDI:000007, BAYLORCD13 20171211 and 20171215, the spikes could not be shown to share the clock of the trial table, neither by a rate change after the onset of delay photostimulation nor by trial-type selectivity after sample onset. The first holds 15 trials for 38 units (8 with photostimulation, and 1 and 4 correct lick-right and lick-left control trials), the second 7 units. The other 52 sessions show it by one or both contrasts.

In DANDI:000007 session BAYLORCD8 20171020 the behavior runs on after the recording ends. Every unit's observation interval ends at 7221.77 s, and the last 127 of the 462 trials, from 7223.1 to 8481.39 s, hold no spike of any unit. The obs_intervals column records this, but an analysis that does not apply it counts those trials as silent.

reconciliation.blind_note: The author run and the three author-revise runs show nothing of gao-2018-01; the audit lines in author.md are the record this attempt wrote. The author-answers run, after the outcomes were recorded, looked for questions/gao-2018.yaml and printed lines 400 to 470 of transcripts/see-2018/author-revise-1.md, which quote the start of gao-2018-01's questions file, including its question on the claims file's E3 and the beginning of its reason, that on these data the preparatory part of Fig. 2c is similar under every epoch while the peak lies in the response epoch only under one. It also printed the first lines of questions/gao-2018.yaml and grep lines of other papers' recorder transcripts that name docs/pilot-notes/gao-2018-01.md, without its content. That run changed no outcome, note, finding or file of the attempt.

outcomes.note: Difference in method. Both attempts get the same pooled result (0.873 to 0.835, one-sided p = 0.108 and 0.107); gao-2018-02 also read the laser traces of CRCNS:alm-4, found two sessions whose light disagrees with code 4, and without them finds a drop (p = 0.042), so it records the absence as holding in part.

Difference in method. gao-2018-01 pooled codes 5 and 6 and judged the bias on CD12 and CD13, the paper's mice, which drop on the same trial type. gao-2018-02 took reading (b) as code 6 alone, from the code descriptions of CRCNS:alm-4, and counted CD8 and CD14 with them, which gives mice biased each way.

Difference in method. Both measured the ALM fraction (0.525 and 0.563); gao-2018-01 blocked the claim as the CN half is missing, and gao-2018-02 recorded the ALM half as a partial result, as the criterion's last sentence allows. The claims check of 2026-11-14 lists no change to this criterion.

Difference in method, as for fig2-preparatory-more-in-alm. gao-2018-01 blocked it for the missing CN half after measuring 0.572 to 0.587 in ALM; gao-2018-02 measured 0.642 and recorded the ALM half as a partial result.

Difference in method, the neurons and trials. gao-2018-01 used all 676 units over the width rule (3.379 and 3.767 spikes/s, below tolerance); gao-2018-02 used the 486 pyramidal neurons that pass the deposited scripts' trial-count rule, with GoodTrials from CRCNS:alm-4 (4.03 and 4.21, within tolerance).

Difference in method, the reading of the criterion. Both find counts above tolerance (158 and 112, 122 and 106) and an increase fraction within 10% of 0.55; gao-2018-01 counted the fraction toward a partial result, gao-2018-02 applied it only where the dataset holds fewer neurons, as the criterion says.

Difference in method. gao-2018-01 judged by most of 20 random draws of the preference trials, on 438 neurons; gao-2018-02 made one draw on 336 neurons with code 6 trials. In earlier_findings.ipynb, with code 6, 8 and 11 of 20 draws meet the criterion, so a single draw can fall either way.

Difference in method, the latency. Both find the recovery fails; gao-2018-01's latency by the paper's method came out at 0.01 to 1.40 ms, outside the tolerance, while gao-2018-02's start label gives 3.30 ms, at its lower bound, so it records a partial result. The claims file also gained a named test for the fastigial comparison on 2026-11-14.

Difference in method, the sessions and trials of the coding direction. gao-2018-01 used 9 fastigial and 13 dentate sessions and found no dentate change; gao-2018-02's session rule keeps 8 and 12 and finds a dentate difference whose interval excludes zero (0.15 to 4.18); in the last 400 ms it includes zero without the sessions whose laser traces disagree with their codes.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The executed notebook of the first run with the summary removed (it had no Result cells then; they were added in this revision), the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier queried both archives and tested hier_boot and latency on synthetic inputs. It gave its own outcome for each claim and disagreed with six (fig1g-dentate-activation-little-effect, fig2-preparatory-more-in-alm, fig3d-alm-altered-by-cn-inhibition, fig3e-alm-increase-decrease, fig3f-alm-selectivity-abolished-by-cn-inhibition, cd-captures-selectivity). It reported no place where the claims file misreads the paper, so no question was added for a reader. Report in transcripts/gao-2018/verifier-1-report.md. The cell numbers in the reasons below are those of the round-1 notebook, not of the current one.

disagreements.reason: Cell 22, no drop at p < 0.05 (p = 0.107, change -0.039). This is an absence claim tested in 3 of 8 mice, with reading (a) only, using a test that is conservative (problem 7).
Only the ALM half can be tested. With all neurons as denominator, 0.538 to 0.563 lies within 0.59 +- 0.059. With selective neurons as denominator, 0.71 to 0.73 lies outside.

Cell 45, latency is 15 to 42 ms under every reading and label, against 7.1 +- 3.8. The count is 228 (all trials) or 106 (correct only), against 197 +- 19.7. The data hold more neurons than the paper (486 tested, 682 pyramidal), so the fraction fallback does not apply. Problem 6 (affects a conclusion), the unit counts do not reconcile with the paper and the lab's compiled lists were not used to reconcile. Problem 9 (does not affect a conclusion), the clock check leaves out the inhibition sessions.

Cell 49, 122/106 (all trials) and 65/41 (correct only), against 108 +- 10.8 and 89 +- 8.9. The increase fraction of 0.535 (all trials) would pass, but the criterion allows the fraction only when the data hold fewer neurons, and here they hold more.

Cell 53, photo-inhibition selectivity is 0.39 [0.19, 0.60] (whole delay) and 0.27 [0.02, 0.53] (last 500 ms). Both intervals exclude 0, also with 5 screening trials. Selectivity is reduced by 73 to 82%, not abolished.

Cell 63, under reading (b) on held-out trials selectivity is 66.3%, within 64.1 +- 3.4. Variance is 35.9 to 38.7% under (b) and 56 to 59% under (a), against 27.0 +- 4.2. It matches only under the notebook's own single-trial variant (problem 2, which is not in the claims file and fits poorly with task-related activity).

The full executed notebook of the author-revise-1 run with its Result cells and summary, the helper module, the entry README, the claims file, the attempt record and the round-1 report. The verifier agreed with 45 of the 46 outcomes and disagreed with fig3f-alm-selectivity-abolished-by-cn-inhibition. paper_notes.statement: The datasets hold more ALM units than the paper reports for the same mice; 1186 units (1084 pyramidal) in the 9 photo-activation mice, where the paper reports 912 pyramidal neurons, and 737 units (682 pyramidal) in the 4 photo-inhibition mice, where it reports 490 units (454 pyramidal) over 19 sessions. The lab's own compiled analysis files deposited with CRCNS:alm-4 (analysis_compile_all_ALM_data.mat, analysis_compiled_all_ALM_DCNstim_FR.mat and analysis_compiled_all_ALM_DCNsilencing_selectivity.mat) hold exactly the deposited units, 1186 and 737 with the same cell types, and 20 photo-inhibition sessions, so they do not record the selection. Which units, and for the photo-inhibition mice which of the 20 sessions, entered the paper's analyses is not stated.

The analysis scripts deposited with CRCNS:alm-4 differ from the Methods in places. The photostimulation selectivity scripts fix each neuron's preferred trial type from 5 trials of each type, where the Methods say 10 for ALM; the coding direction script averages cd_t over windows starting from 3.0 s to 0.4 s before the go cue (pre-sample, sample and delay), where the Methods say the delay epoch; the selectivity test uses correct trials in the Fig. 2 script and correct and error trials in the photostimulation scripts. The coding direction compile (analysis_compiled_all_ALM_DCNstim_CD.mat) holds 23 sessions with 8 to 46 neurons, where the Methods give 28 of 39 sessions with that range; it keeps sessions with at least 3 trials per condition (the Methods say more than 5) and estimates the cd from all control trials but as many as the photostimulation trials of each type, not from a half. It declares the variables for the variance captured by the cd but never computes them.

For the response latencies (4.5, 8.3 and 7.1 ms), how is a 10 ms bin placed in time (start, centre or end) and which window decides that a neuron is significantly modulated? Labelling by start gives 3.64 ms for fastigial and 3.30 ms for dentate photo-activation, by centre 8.64 and 8.30 ms. Only the start label matches both reported values, the dentate one at the lower bound of 8.3 +- 5.0; for CN photo-inhibition every choice gives 15 ms or more against 7.1.

For the fractions captured by the coding direction (64.1% of selectivity, 27.0% of variance), are they ratios of RMS or of squared RMS, is selectivity measured on the trials that estimated the cd or on independent ones, and is activity variance over single trials or condition means? Only squared ratios on independent trials with single-trial variance give both values here (66.3% and 28.4%); other combinations give 73% to 85% and 36% to 59%.

Which neurons were tested for photostimulation effects (the minimum numbers of control and photostimulation trials) and which sessions entered the coding direction analysis? With the deposited scripts' rules 177 to 190 ALM neurons are modulated by fastigial photo-activation (paper 227) and 20 of 34 sessions enter the coding direction analysis (paper 28 of 39).

For the population selectivity of Fig. 2c (E3), which epoch fixes each neuron's preferred trial type? It decides where the maximum lies; on 1274 selective ALM neurons it lies 0.24 to 0.49 s after the go cue when the response epoch fixes the preference, 0.06 to 0.23 s before it with the delay epoch, and in the sample epoch in 9 of 10 draws with the sample epoch. For Fig. 3f the random draw of the screening trials can decide the outcome; on trials with photostimulation code 6, 8 of 20 draws with 5 screening trials of each type and 11 of 20 with 10 of each give a photo-inhibition selectivity whose bootstrap interval includes zero.

entries.name: gao-2018
entries.title: A cortico-cerebellar loop for motor planning (Gao et al. 2018)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Gao, Davis, Thomas, Economo, Abrego, Svoboda, De Zeeuw and Li (2018) on its two deposits, DANDI:000007 and CRCNS:alm-4, which hold the same 54 ALM recording sessions of 13 mice during fastigial or dentate photo-activation and CN photo-inhibition. It tests the behavior in those sessions, ALM trial-type selectivity, ALM responses to CN photostimulation and the coding direction analysis. The lesion experiments, CN recordings, lick times, VGAT-ChR2 experiments and anatomy are not deposited.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Gao et al. (2018) from DANDI:000007 and CRCNS:alm-4
The findings of attempt gao-2018-01, checked on DANDI:000007 version 0.220126.1903
